blocks.title: Therapeutic window
blocks.text: The therapeutic window is the range of drug concentrations in the plasma that are effective without causing harmful side effects. It is the 'sweet spot' of a medicine: not too low to be ineffective and not too high to be dangerous.

items: Minimum effective concentration (MEC): the lowest level of the drug below which it fails to produce a clinical effect.
Minimum toxic concentration (MTC): the lowest level at which the drug begins to cause adverse effects, or 'poisoning'.
Duration of action: the time for which the drug concentration stays within its therapeutic window.

blocks.text: A wide therapeutic window means the drug has generous safety limits, because there is a large gap between the dose that works and the dose that harms; this allows more flexibility in dosing. A narrow window means the drug is less safe, because the effective dose is very close to the toxic dose. Doctors must be very careful when prescribing such drugs and often check the patient's blood to keep the drug level within the narrow range. Taking several medicines together, genetic factors, obesity, age or general health can also change a drug's therapeutic window, because they affect the drug's metabolism and efficacy.

blocks.alt: Top: two S-shaped curves of patients responding against dose: efficacy (blue) rises first, with ED50 marked; toxicity (red) rises at higher doses, with TD50 marked; a green band between them is the therapeutic window, and TI = TD50/ED50. Bottom: the drug level in the blood rises after one dose and then falls; a red dashed line marks the MTC and a green dashed line the MEC; the band between them is the therapeutic window, and an arrow marks the duration of action while the level is above the MEC.
blocks.caption: Therapeutic window and therapeutic index (original diagram after Figure 32.1).
blocks.long_description: A drug helps when its level is above the MEC and harms when it rises above the MTC. The further apart the efficacy and toxicity curves are, the wider the window and the safer the drug.
